case_title: State of Haryana v. Krishan & Anr.
aggravating_circumstances: Sale of poisonous liquor, attempt to destroy evidence
trial_court_outcome: Convicted of culpable homicide and other charges
neutral_facts: The prosecution case centered around a tragic incident where 36 persons died and 44 persons lost their eyesight after consuming spurious liquor purchased from a licensed liquor vend. Medical evidence confirmed that the cause of death and loss of vision was due to the consumption of liquor adulterated with methyl alcohol. Victims and their relatives stated they purchased the liquor from the respondents' vend, which was corroborated by the conduct of the respondents in disposing of remaining stock after the incident. The prosecution presented evidence showing the respondents were licensed vendors and that they had knowledge of the harmful effects of the liquor they sold. The trial court convicted the respondents for their involvement in the sale of spurious liquor, while the High Court initially acquitted them, citing lack of evidence. The Supreme Court overturned the High Court's acquittal, finding sufficient evidence to connect the respondents to the tragedy.
